title: Choose the visual world for Food Rescue Network
question: The roll assigned The Ticket Rail. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Ticket Rail
options.lineage: commercial kitchen order tickets on a steel rail
options.thesis: Every rescue is a numbered kitchen ticket: fired, claimed, run, and stamped delivered.
options.viewport: A steel rail crosses the page with three live tickets clipped to it, under a condensed headline and a red Fire a ticket action.
options.risk: Tickets can tip into costume if the tear edges and stamps act out on every screen instead of only at state changes.

raised.raise: Colour lives only on ticket edges and stamps; every reading field stays ink on paper.
Each ticket stacks its milestones as stamped courses, so history reads as one accumulated record.
Hierarchy by scale contrast alone: huge ticket numbers against small mono print, no decorative containers.
Every rescue is addressed by one ticket number, printed identically on every screen.
Urgency gets billing weight: the pickup deadline sets larger as it nears.
Impact figures are drawn as flat ruled bars, never stat tiles.

options.label: Dabba Codes
options.thesis: Every rescue carries a painted route code read at each relay handoff.
options.viewport: A grid of steel tiffin lids painted with route codes beside a heavy headline and a black Report action.
options.risk: The dabbawala is the most familiar metaphor for Indian food logistics, so it reads as expected.

options.label: Iridescent Cloud Edge
options.thesis: Quiet white fields with colour only at the edge.
options.viewport: White field, spectral band on the active edge.
options.case: Loses both axes: kitchens and drivers do not see themselves in weather optics.
options.kept: Colour confined to edges; text stays achromatic.

options.label: Coiled Earth Tower
options.thesis: Progress as courses rising one coil at a time.
options.viewport: Banded courses of clay rising behind the headline.
options.case: Loses both axes: the rescue flow is a relay, not a slow build.
options.risk: Heavy and slow for a time-critical task.

options.label: Variable Font Specimen
options.viewport: One giant glyph and a breathing grid.
options.case: Loses both axes: nothing about food rescue lives in a type specimen.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.case: Loses both axes: retro broadcast is foreign to the audience and hurts phone readability.
options.kept: One ticket number addresses each rescue everywhere.

options.label: Soundsystem Dance Poster
options.viewport: Ranked block caps over a hand-ruled date grid.
options.case: Loses both axes: too loud for daily operational screens.

options.label: Du Bois Data Portraits
options.viewport: A crimson spiral of meals delivered.
options.case: Loses both axes: strong for impact, but foreign to the audience and silent about the workflow.
options.kept: Impact drawn as flat ruled bars.
options.risk: Only one section has data to argue with.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean nonprofit platform page, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and Report action beside a photo, three feature cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other food-donation platform by design.
